mainEntity.name: How do I know if my cabin interior is a good candidate for staining?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabin interior staining is best when the wood is sound, dry, and free of heavy grease, mildew, or active water damage. If the cabin has soft spots, peeling finish, or moisture staining, those issues should be addressed before staining so the new finish bonds properly and lasts longer.
acceptedAnswer.description: A cabin interior is a good staining candidate when the wood is solid, dry, and properly cleaned. Damage, moisture issues, or heavy finish failure should be repaired first so the stain adheres evenly and performs well.
